$comment: Asset rules read by validate.py and the export scripts (DESIGN 19.2-19.4). Names use shell globs (fnmatch; case-sensitive except marker patterns). A material is named by its engine_name custom property when it has one (LIB_PaintedPlate -> Hull), else by its own name. Triangle ranges are LOD0 [min, max]; texture is the largest side in px; size is the bounding box in metres along 'axis' (max = longest side, z = height).

reference.$comment: DESIGN 19.2: a 1 m grid and a 1.85 m biped are the scale references in every file. They live in a top-level collection the export never writes.

fits.why: art bible 1: doorways are at least 2.4 m tall x 1.4 m wide

lod.$comment: DESIGN 19.2: four LODs per asset, LOD3 under 5% of LOD0. LODs are collections (sources) or nodes (exports) named <variant>_LOD<n>. generateRatios are the decimation targets the export uses when no LODs were hand-made.

names.$comment: Object, collection and material names. Blender's .001 uniqueness suffixes are stripped from exported node and mesh names; materials export under their engine_name or their own name.

markers.why: colliders are simple boxes or hulls the game hides
point lights; the game reads the extras
blinking lamp; its child mesh is the lens
rotating part; its child mesh spins
weapon hardpoint, size in the name (DESIGN 19.4, art bible 8)
docking or hangar bay (DESIGN 19.4, art bible 8)
where a weapon module attaches to a hardpoint

pbr.why: DESIGN 19.2: base colour, roughness, metallic, normal, ambient occlusion, emissive

glass.why: glass (LIB_Glass): constant colour and roughness allowed; reflection does the work

signal.why: engine-driven glow (engine exhaust, nav lights, lamps): the game scales the glow, the colour comes from the model

effect.why: ability effect meshes are emissive and translucent

decal.why: glyph patterns, liveries and icons are texture sets

library.why: library materials drive base colour, roughness and normal from nodes (procedural is fine: each asset bakes its own copy, AO included)

textures.$comment: P1.E14.T12: exported maps are KTX2 (Basis Universal) behind KHR_texture_basisu with full mip chains, so a 4k hero downloads in tens of MB and stays compressed on the GPU (artlib/ktx.py, encoder: KTX-Software's ktx). codec per glTF slot (metallicRoughness, other = extension slots): uastc (RDO, then Zstandard) keeps gradients and data exact enough for normals; etc1s (BasisLZ) is several times smaller for colour and AO. A family may set its own "textures" (e.g. {"compress": false}) to export PNGs, which the validator then accepts for it. Each class's gpuTextureMB is what one variant's maps may take on the GPU once transcoded (8 bits a texel, mips included).

hero.why: DESIGN 19.2: player bodies, hulls, Wardens, the Patient, each capital's landmarks

npc.why: not in 19.2: crews and city NPCs share the player skeleton but are seen in groups, so between creature and hero

viewmodel.why: not in 19.2: first-person arms and tools are always at arm's length, so one LOD and creature-level texel density

building.why: not in 19.2 (textures are: 2k): whole buildings, station modules and sites sit between props and heroes

kit.why: not in 19.2: modular kit pieces (walls, bridges, gates, lamps) share a 2k atlas per kit

weapon.why: not in 19.2: hardpoint modules are seen beside the hull in chase view, so above props

flora_tree.why: not in 19.2: trees are instanced by the hundred and hand over to impostors beyond 400 m

flora.why: not in 19.2: bushes, plants, grass, rocks, crystals and deposits are instanced by the thousand

effect.why: not in 19.2: ability effect meshes are short-lived and mostly emissive

cosmetic.why: not in 19.2: glyph patterns, liveries and title icons are texture sets on carrier planes

library.why: the shared material library (assets/blend/_library.blend): materials and references only

characters.what: player bodies (3 peoples), head and crest variants, suit sets, first-person arms and tools

npcs.what: crews, Quiet Table agents, the Quartermaster, city NPCs

hulls.what: the 13 hulls with liveries, gear, canopy, cockpit interior, damage and husked variants

materials.why: DESIGN 10.4 and 19.4: liveries, recolours, husked variants, traffic and wrecks read these names (after engine_name)

weapons.what: the 8 hardpoint weapon modules as mountable meshes

requiredMarkers.why: aligns the module to a hull's HP_ empty

cities.what: the three building kits, civic buildings, gates, walls, bridges, lamps and the anchor stone landmarks

requiredMarkers.why: the walker collides with every city piece

stations.what: the modular Waystation kit, the Scrapyard kit and the Hive

requiredMarkers.why: ships and walkers collide with station modules

sites.what: outposts, monoliths, beacons, crash sites, dens, Cartographer vaults, glyph stones

requiredMarkers.why: Structures.js turns COL_ meshes into colliders
every site is something the player interacts with

creatures.what: the five body plans, predators, stone-touched overlays, horrors, grazers, lurkers, leviathans
creatures.why: Fauna.js animates crowds from _limb/_pivot/_glow in the vertex shader and recolours species from the colour-region mask

constructs.what: outpost drone, Overseer, monolith sentinel, the Wardens, the sentinel ship

bosses.what: Pack Alpha, Herd Mother, Sentinel Primes, the Dreadnought, the Patient, the Hive Heart, Husk Admiral, Brood Mother
bosses.why: DESIGN 19.2: hero creatures and bosses are fully skinned

flora.what: the flora library, resource plants and formations
flora.why: floraModels.js recolours each kind from the colour-region mask (R primary, G secondary, B accent, A occlusion)

props.what: cargo and loot pods, ammo, catalysts, market stalls, terminals, the Recall glyph set

cosmetics.what: glyph patterns for suits and hulls, liveries, title icons

cutscenes.what: cutscene camera paths, dialogue, events and actors, one cutscene a .blend (DESIGN 19.2, 19.4; art bible 8: CAM_<cutscene>_<shot>)
cutscenes.why: a camera-only file: validate.py runs export_cutscene.py's naming and marker-grammar checks (the rules the client's parseCutscene applies) instead of the mesh checks; export_cutscene.py, not art:export, writes the JSON

legacy.$comment: The demo's script-built exports (packages/client/public/models/*.glb). They predate these rules and are expected to fail until their families are rebuilt (P1.E14.T07 deletes the generators).
